summary: Discovery call focused on embedding & rerank pilot: integration with customer's vector DB, throughput targets (200 qps read), dimensionality tradeoffs (512 vs 768), hybrid search / topK rerank strategy, hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC) and security/compliance requirements. Action items include pilot template, sample data, and benchmark plan.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can folks do quick intros?
[00:06] Jordan (Bluewave): Jordan here, I run the search product.
[00:09] Priya (Bluewave): Priya, infra/ML ops.
[00:11] Ethan (Bluewave): Ethan, CTO, popping in for the first 15.
[00:15] Ravi (Bluewave): Ravi from security.
[00:17] Samir: Great. Maya and Luca from Redwood on the line — Maya will lead the technical bits.
[00:22] Maya (Redwood): Hi all, excited to dig in. Quick agenda: understand current stack, numbers, constraints, and success criteria for a pilot.
[00:30] Jordan: Quick context: we power search across customer docs and product content. Currently using an in-house vector index backed by Milvus for nearest-neighbor, and a late-stage reranker that does cross-encoder scoring. Latency and cost are creeping up as query volume grows. We want to evaluate Redwood for either hosted inference + keep our DB, or move to a Dedicated pool / Private deployment.
[00:48] Samir: Perfect — couple of clarifying q's: target QPS? p95/p99 targets? and how big are vectors today? dims and count?
[00:55] Jordan: Target is 200 QPS steady-state, with spikes to 400 during business hours. p95 ideally < 150ms end-to-end for a topk=10 retrieval+rerank; p99 < 400ms. Vectors today are 768 dims, about 8 million vectors.
[01:18] Priya: We shard across 6 Milvus nodes, replication 2. On the reranker we run a small cross encoder for top 20 results, that costs a lot. The idea is maybe we do a cheaper embed-based pre-score and then a smaller rerank.
[01:32] Maya: Got it — so the common pattern is hybrid retrieval: ANN topK from vector DB + Redwood for scalar rerank or full-model rerank depending on cost. A few questions: are you open to lowering dim to 512 if it materially reduces cost and improves throughput? and are you constrained on sending vectors to hosted vendors?
[01:52] Jordan: We'd prefer not to send PII off-prem for now — customer data policy. That's why Dedicated or Private is interesting. Security will be a gating factor.
[02:02] Ravi: To add, for any hosted option we need SOC 2, SAML SSO, KMS-based envelope encryption, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also need data residency in US-EAST for the pilot.
[02:16] Luca (Redwood): We support SOC 2 + enterprise SAML and KMS integrations. For Hosted we can offer region pinning to us-east and customer-level retention. For Dedicated you get a reserved GPU pool with VPC peering; for Private we can run our control plane in your VPC — both satisfy the no-data-exit requirement.
[02:34] Priya: Perf-wise, curious about throughput for 512 vs 768 dims and what batching/kv cache options you have. We do a lot of short queries (mean tokens 12) and rely on heavy batching for rerank.
[02:47] Maya: On the runtime side: for pure embedding generation, 512 dims will typically reduce memory and compute and improves throughput ~20-35% depending on model and quantization. For rerank we often recommend a two-tier approach: 1) cheap dot-product scoring of existing dense vectors to produce topN (30-50), 2) Redwood does a focused rerank pass on topK (8-20) using a smaller cross encoder or distilled reranker — this balances cost and latency.
[03:15] Jordan: If we keep Milvus as the vector store, what's the integration pattern? Do we call Redwood for rerank only and keep retrieval local? Or do you recommend copying vectors into Redwood-managed index?
[03:27] Maya: Both are supported. Typical pilot: keep Milvus for retrieval, call Redwood for rerank via API. If you want higher end-to-end SLAs and simplified ops we can suggest Dedicated with our managed index or Private with our index running in your VPC. Copying vectors into Redwood-managed index helps us optimize sharding and co-location for low tail latency, but it's optional.
[03:46] Priya: How do you handle KV cache and prefix cache when doing reranks? We see lots of repeated queries and warm prefixes.
[03:53] Luca: We do automatic KV caching for generative tasks. For rerank/cross-encoders it's less about prefix cache and more about batching and model warm pools. But for multi-step flows (embedding -> retrieval -> rerank) we can cache embeddings or topK results to reduce calls.
[04:08] Ethan: Pricing — speak plainly. We need predictable numbers for pilot and to compare to our in-house cost.
[04:14] Samir: We'll send a pilot pricing sheet — flat monthly for Dedicated baseline, and usage-based for Hosted with volume discounts. For hybrid approach we can estimate per-rerank compute and per-embed compute. We'll include an example TCO for 200 qps and 8M vectors.
[04:29] Jordan: On sharding: with 8M vectors at 768 dims, what's typical memory footprint and recommended replica count to hit 200 QPS p99 under 200ms?
[04:38] Maya: Rough heuristics: 768 float32 unquantized is heavy — you'd want 4–8 TB of memory across nodes. With 8-bit or 4-bit quantization and using optimized ANN (IVF/HNSW with product quant) you can shrink it 4–8x. For 200 QPS and low p99 you'd probably run 3 replicas with sharding to distribute CPU/IO. If you want strict p99 < 200ms we'd recommend Dedicated with co-located reranker to avoid cross-network hops.
[05:08] Priya: You mentioned quantization — do we need to re-embed if we quantize?
[05:12] Maya: Quantization is on the index side, not the embedding model outputs. You index the same vectors but store them in quantized form in the vector DB. If you switch to a lower-dim backbone model (e.g., 512-dim), you'd re-embed, which we can help measure for quality vs latency tradeoffs.
[05:29] Jordan: Quality question: our relevance metric is MR@10 and we saw a drop when we tried distilled embeddings last year. How do you recommend evaluating quality with lower dims?
[05:38] Maya: Best practice: run an offline A/B with a labeled eval set — we can run pairwise comparisons on your 1k (or 5k) queries and compute MR/ndcg deltas. For the pilot, provide a 1k query set + judged relevances; we'll run candidate topK retrievals for 512 vs 768 and the rerank step and show relative delta.
[05:56] Jordan: Sounds good. Also, we need to check the rerank latency split — most of our p99 comes from the cross-encoder. If we do partial rerank (e.g., smaller transformer), what's the latency profile?
[06:06] Maya: Distilled rerankers (small transformer, ~20–60 ms per item on GPU depending on batch) can reduce per-item cost. If you rerank top10 with batch=10 you can often get aggregate rerank < 150ms on GPU. For CPU-only Dedicated deployments it will be higher. We can scope the exact numbers in the benchmark.
[06:28] Ravi: For security, KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? And audit logs format?
[06:33] Luca: Yes, customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we support CMK integration (envelope encryption) and export logs to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder. We also support SAML SSO and role-based access controls.
[06:47] Priya: Network connectivity: if we go Dedicated/VPC peering, what's the expected egress pattern? Will traffic stay in our VPC?
[06:54] Maya: With VPC peering and Private options, inference traffic stays inbound to your VPC, and you control egress. For Dedicated we typically set up peering and NAT routing so data doesn't traverse public internet. For Private deployments we can run the entire stack inside your network.
[07:08] Jordan: Any gotchas with cold-starts / model warm pools? We see latency spikes in the morning.
[07:13] Maya: We support warm pools and pre-warmed replicas for scheduled spikes; autoscaling can be tuned for warm start thresholds. Also, persistent KV caches for repeated prefixes reduce cold-start impact.
[07:24] Ethan: What about fallback strategies? If Redwood Dedicated capacity is constrained, do you route to smaller models or another region?
[07:32] Samir: We have smart routing: you can configure fallbacks — e.g., route to a cheaper quantized variant or fallback to a hosted lower-SLA endpoint. For mission-critical flows you can maintain a small on-prem replica as emergency fallback.
[07:44] Priya: For the pilot benchmark, we want to run an end-to-end test including Milvus retrieval + Redwood rerank at 200 qps for 10 minutes to measure p95/p99. What do you need from us?
[07:53] Maya: We'll need: a) 100k vector snapshot (or a representative shard), b) 1k representative queries, c) desired topK, and d) network topology (VPC/peering info). We'll propose infra and a runbook.
[08:06] Jordan: We'll try to provide 100k vectors and 1k queries by Thursday.
[08:10] Samir: Great. We'll also include a pricing comparsion and a pilot contract with limited-term credits.
[08:16] Ravi: One more on compliance: can you share SOC 2 cert and pen test report? Also need a data processing addendum (DPA).
[08:23] Luca: Yes we'll share SOC 2, pen test summary, and our standard DPA — Samir will attach those to the follow-up.
[08:30] Maya: Quick technical note: for reranking we recommend batching the cross-encoder calls per query across the topK, and we can run model parallelization if you need extreme throughput. Also, consider using an embedding-based lightweight scorer for initial pruning to reduce cross-encoder calls.
[08:48] Priya: Regarding dims — can Redwood run an embedding delta test (same docs, 512 vs 768) and give us embedding distance statistics and recall@k?
[08:58] Maya: Absolutely — that's part of the pilot. We'll run both offline and online A/B if you want.
[09:03] Jordan: Ok, last two practical items: SLA expectations for Dedicated and Private, and who to loop in for procurement.
[09:10] Samir: Dedicated comes with an SLA for throughput/uptime depending on committed capacity; Private has a support contract. For procurement, loop in your procurement and legal — we'll provide contracts and an initial SOW.
[09:22] Ethan: I'll have procurement reach out.
[09:24] Samir: Quick recap of next steps: Samir sends pilot template + SOC2/DPA; Maya sends benchmark plan; Priya sends data sample; schedule a 60-min tech run next week with Priya and Maya to execute the 200 QPS test. Anything else?
[09:38] Jordan: That covers it. Thanks.
[09:41] Ravi: Thanks.
[09:42] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email.
[09:45] Samir: End.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional overlapped talk; model/term names sometimes auto-transcribed (e.g., Milvus heard as "Millviews" in a couple spots).
